title: Indiana Monthly Water Resource Summary — August 2026
summary: Precipitation: During August 2026, Indiana’s average precipitation was well above normal, with a statewide monthly precipitation average of 200 percent normal. Drought Monitor: For September 8, 2026, the U.S. Drought Monitor shows isolated spots of “abnormally dry” conditions in the southwest and south-central part of the state and no drought conditions for the rest of Indiana. The U.S. Seasonal Drought Outlook predicts no drought conditions through at least the end of November 2026. Streamflow: In August 2026, all twelve of the twelve streams included in drought reporting since 1999 had above normal to significantly above normal stream flow. Eel River at North Manchester had the lowest mean monthly flow at 116%, and the Whitewater River near Alpine had the highest mean monthly flow at 1554%. Groundwater: As of August 31, 2026, new water level data is available for all nine wells currently monitored. Data indicates that water level is above normal for four of the nine wells: Vigo 7, Morgan 4, Randolph 3, and Posey 3. Data indicates that the water level is near normal for Laporte 9, Fulton 7, Clark 20, and Harrison 8; and water level remains well below normal for LaGrange 2.

title: Indiana Monthly Water Resource Summary — October 2026
summary: Precipitation: During October 2026, Indiana’s average precipitation was much below normal, with a statewide monthly precipitation average of 41.6 percent normal. Drought Monitor: For November 3, 2026, the U.S. Drought Monitor shows most of Indiana is experiencing “Abnormally Dry” or “Moderate Drought” conditions and no drought conditions for north-central, northeast and east-central portions of Indiana. The U.S. Seasonal Drought Outlook predicts drought conditions to persist for the west-central, central and a small area in the southeast through at least the end of January 2027. Streamflow: In October 2026, three of the twelve streams included in drought reporting since 1999 had near to above normal stream flow. Muscatatuck River near Deputy had the lowest mean monthly flow at 3%, and the Kankakee River at Shelby had the highest mean monthly flow at 157%. Groundwater: As of October 31, 2026, new water level data is available for all nine wells currently monitored. Data indicates that water level is above normal for one of the nine wells: Morgan 4. Data indicates that the water level is near normal for Laporte 9, Fulton 7, Vigo 7, Randolph 3, Posey 3, and Harrison 8; and water level remains below to well below normal for LaGrange 2 and Clark 20.
